pr_title: Add checks for exception loops through suppressed exceptions only
pr_body:
Refactor how nested exceptions are serialized to prevent a SOF when recursive suppressed exceptions are serialized.

This fixes #93943
pr_comments: Hi @thecoop, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
I'm thinking this should probably be backported to 7.17, and all supported 8.x?

I considered that, but I really don't want to put a public method on `ElasticsearchException` with a really weird additional parameter, to support a different class in another package. With `ThreadLocal`, it is all kept private & hidden, with no additional effects elsewhere.

I see your point that the additional method would have to be added just because `StreamOutput` needs this. The `writeTo` method is there just for the serialisation in StreamOutput too. You might argue, that perhaps serialisation logic could be in `StreamOutput/Input` as it is for other primitives types. With that you would not have to keep `writeTo` and `writeTo2-with level`.  But I would not go that far. 

`ThreadLocal` approach seems fragile to me - it would be easy to miss the increase/decrease - the actual problem is actually hidden deeply in `StreamOutput:L1112`. 
But most importantly it is hard to understand. I can see why it was used now, but not without debugging. 
I would prefer we avoid this.

The ThreadLocal shouldn't lose anything, as every increment is balanced with a decrement. I'm not sure what other ways to solve this are other than a ThreadLocal or adding a new public method just for this functionality (well, apart from a complete refactor, which seems overkill)

I share Przemek's concerns about ThreadLocals. Their fragility is demonstrated in this PR by the hack necessary to save/reset it for an internal call. We should avoid using them.

I think instead we can solve this by moving the all exception writing code into ElasticsearchException, so that there is a single public method for writing a Throwable?  Then an internal method can still exist which keeps track of the stack depth. That method can then be delegated to in StreamOutput.writeException.

I've re-done the implementation & moved things around between `StreamOutput` and `ElasticsearchException`.

The result is somewhat cumbersome, due to the following constraints:

1. Maintaining the same public API
2. Keeping `nestedLevel` within `ElasticsearchException`, but maintaining it through all recursive calls
3. Keeping the serialization of id for various exception types within `StreamOutput`, to maintain the counterpart with the deserialization code in `StreamInput`
4. Keeping a hook for tests to assert properties of the exceptions when the nested limit is reached.

It looks like the `rootException` parameter may not still be needed, and the assertions around that are superfluous, but we still need a way for tests to disable the assertion. Or we just remove the assertion completely, and rely on the `IllegalStateException`?

I think we can relax some of the constraints you mention:

> 1. Maintaining the same public API

This is internal to ES, so change any of these public APIs as necessary.

> 3. Keeping the serialization of id for various exception types within StreamOutput, to maintain the counterpart with the deserialization code in StreamInput

I think it would actually be clearer for ElasticsearchException to handle *all* exception read/write. So I would move the StreamInput and StreamOutput code into ElasticsearchException. The only reason I suggested delegating the existing method in StreamOutput was to minimize the impact of the change to existing callers, but the implementation on both sides can be moved.

> 4. Keeping a hook for tests to assert properties of the exceptions when the nested limit is reached.

This is tricky. I see the purpose of the assertion, to get earlier feedback in tests if we have a circular exception chain, but I'm not sure it is worth keeping as is. I suggest removing the test from the buffer classes, making a package private version of ElasticsearchException.writeException with which you can control this assertion, and testing in a unit test in ElasticsearchExceptionTests.
I've moved round the exception mechanisms. I had forgot to actually serialise the ElasticsearchException data, so that's added now too.
I think this is too big a change to backport, we might just need to leave it in previous versions.
My only concern about backporting is the size of the change & the number of files modified, it increases the chance of conflicts & regressions. If that's not a concern here, that's fine.

issue_context.title: ElasticsearchException.writeStackTraces does not check nested depth of suppressed exceptions
issue_context.body:
Whilst `StreamOutput.writeException` does keep track of the nested depth of causal exceptions, `ElasticsearchException` doesn't use this for suppressed exceptions. This means it is possible for `StreamOutput.writeException` to throw a stack overflow when writing out very deeply nested suppressed exceptions, or a loop of suppressed exceptions (however that occurred).

This bug is present on 7.17 as well as 8.x branches

review_comments:
For the nested exception callback to be as useful as before, I think the default here needs to have the same assert. The reason we have an assert at all is so we can fail explicitly when in tests.

However, I'm also on the fence about whether such an assertion is actually useful. We would only get it when running unit/integ tests, but not when running rest tests. We can discuss as a followup though.
